title: RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT (RRD): CLINICAL MASTERY
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the diagnosis, staging, and surgical management of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment. This poster outlines the critical decision-making processes required for successful anatomical and functional reattachment.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: RRD is the separation of the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) via a full-thickness retinal break (tear or hole) allowing fluid from the vitreous cavity into the subretinal space. Incidence is approx. 1 in 10,000 per year. Peak incidence: 50-70 years old.

sections.title: Clinical Features & Symptoms
content: Floaters: Sudden onset of 'cobwebs' or dark spots (Weiss ring).
Visual Field Defect: Peripheral 'curtain' or 'shadow' encroaching.
Central Vision Loss: Occurs if the macula becomes detached.
RAPD: Present if extensive detachment causes significant ganglion cell loss.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Action Required
content: Macula-ON Detachment: Ocular emergency—prevent progression to macula-OFF.
Severe Vitreous Hemorrhage: Masking the view of the retina.
PVR (Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy) Grade C or worse.
Chronicity signs: Macular cysts or subretinal lines indicating long-standing detachment.

rows: Concave shape, no break, fibrovascular bands

content.explanation: Symptomatic, Traumatic, Aphakic/Pseudophakic, Myopic, Peripheral thinning/Lattice (high risk).

sections.title: Surgical Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Identify break with scleral depression.
Step 3: Scleral Buckle (for phakic, younger patients).
Step 4: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) (for complex/posterior breaks).
Step 5: Tamponade (C3F8, SF6, or Silicone Oil).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always perform 360-degree scleral depressed exam in the fellow eye.
Macula-ON status must be documented with time of onset.
In PPV, use perfluorocarbon liquids (PFCL) to stabilize the posterior pole during membrane peeling.
Prognosis: Visual recovery is heavily dependent on the duration of macular detachment.
